title: Tryouts and Group Chat
premise: Orsen Ravensworth, a senior debate champion at Hollowmere Academy, has perfected the art of being agreeable at home and invisible at school — until the academy's legendary ghost begins leaving him handwritten notes in ink that shouldn't exist, each one naming a student who vanished from the records decades ago. Following the notes into the school's sealed archives, Orsen uncovers a cover-up by the founding board: students quietly expelled and erased to protect a donor family's reputation, a legacy his own grandfather helped bury. As the final game of the season approaches and the board moves to demolish the archive wing, Orsen must choose between the loyalty that has kept his family comfortable and the truth that could free everyone still trapped by the silence. He reads the erased names aloud at the championship assembly, ending the haunting — and his own invisibility.
about_author: Zephyrine Oyelaran is a former high-school debater who grew up above her grandmother's bookshop, where she learned that every family keeps one story locked in the back room. She writes young adult fiction about quiet kids who find their voices in impossible places.

chapters.title: The Art of Agreeing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet him mid-debate tournament, winning effortlessly, then coming home to lose gracefully to his father's plans for his future. Establishes his invisibility strategy and the countdown calendar to graduation. Emotional beat: suffocating competence — he wins everywhere except where it matters.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Rules
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A tour of Hollowmere Academy's hierarchies: the legacy kids, the scholarship kids, and the legend of the Grey Archivist, a ghost said to haunt the old library wing. His best friend Priya dares him to care about something for once. Beat: restless boredom masking fear of standing out.

chapters.title: First Note
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. After debate practice he finds a note in his locker: 'You argue beautifully, Orsen Ravensworth. Ask about Elias.' The ink is silver-grey and cold to the touch; no one was in the hallway. Beat: the first crack in his carefully managed invisibility — someone sees him.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Orsen shows Priya the note; she tests the ink chemically for the school paper and it matches no known compound. They argue about whether it's a prank targeting him specifically. Beat: skeptical excitement — friendship deepening as they investigate together.

chapters.title: Ask About Elias
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He asks his grandfather, a former board member, casually about an 'Elias' from Hollowmere history. Grandfather's teacup pauses mid-air; the subject is shut down with unusual force. Beat: dread — the name means something, and the people closest to him are guarding it.

chapters.title: Second Note
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A second note appears inside his locked debate case: 'Elias Okonkwo. 1974. Not transferred. Erased.' It includes a partial student ID number. Orsen realizes the ghost isn't haunting the school — it's haunting the record. Beat: the mystery becomes personal and urgent.

chapters.title: The Sealed Wing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen and Priya scout the condemned archive wing after hours, finding the door freshly padlocked despite the demolition vote being weeks away. Someone is actively keeping people out. Beat: escalating stakes — this is no longer a ghost story but a cover-up with living guards.

chapters.title: Home Game
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At dinner, his father announces the Ravensworth family will co-chair the archive demolition fundraiser — a legacy honor. Orsen almost objects, then swallows it, hating himself. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes; the enemy may share his table.

chapters.title: Third Note
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The third note names three more erased students, all scholarship kids from the same years, all gone after 'the Whitmore gift.' Orsen cross-references yearbooks: their photos have been razored out. Beat: grief and fury — erasure as violence, made physical.

chapters.title: Priya's Story
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals why she cares so much: her aunt attended Hollowmere on scholarship in the eighties and never spoke of it. She agrees to risk her editorship to publish if they find proof. Beat: shared inheritance of silence; the alliance becomes a mission.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen attends an open board session as debate practice and watches his grandfather deflect a question about archival records with practiced charm. He recognizes the technique — it's the one he uses at home. Beat: horrified recognition; he's been trained by the people he may need to defeat.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sneaking into the wing during a storm, Orsen and Priya get trapped when a caretaker locks the outer door. Inside they find the ghost's nest: decades of notes, clippings, and a ledger of every erased name. Beat: terror turning to awe — the archivist has been waiting for a reader.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Reading the ledger by flashlight, Orsen finds his grandfather's signature on the 1974 expulsion orders — and learns Elias Okonkwo died by suicide after his erasure. Beat: devastation; the abstract mystery becomes a body, a name, a life his family helped destroy.

chapters.title: The Caretaker
chapters.summary: Caretaker Marisol Vega's POV. Caught, the kids expect punishment — instead Marisol reveals she's been leaving food and fresh paper in the wing for thirty years, and that the 'ghost' is real to her too. Beat: unexpected ally; the haunting has had a witness all along.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Version
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts his grandfather privately with the signature. The old man doesn't deny it — he explains it as protection, order, kindness even, and asks Orsen to think of the family. Beat: the seduction of complicity; Orsen understands how good people bury things.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen stops updating his graduation countdown. His debate coach notices he's arguing to win again instead of arguing to be liked. Beat: transformation — invisibility was a choice, and he's choosing differently now, at real cost to his home life.

chapters.title: Demolition Moved Up
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The board accelerates demolition to the day before the championship game — clearly aimed at whoever has been in the wing. Marisol warns them they'll have one night to remove everything. Beat: ticking clock; the institution fights back through logistics, not confrontation.

chapters.title: The Last Night of the Wing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen, Priya, and Marisol evacuate the ledger and evidence as bulldozers arrive at dawn. In the chaos, Orsen finally meets the archivist — Elias's sister, Adaeze, who faked her way onto staff for decades to guard the record. Beat: the ghost given flesh; grief and resolve fused.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. His father discovers the missing ledger and gives Orsen an ultimatum: return it or lose the family's support through college. Orsen, for the first time, argues at home — and loses the argument and wins himself. Beat: climax of the domestic thread; severance accepted.

chapters.title: Championship Day
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Hollowmere wins the final game, the gym packed, cameras rolling. Orsen takes the microphone during the awards assembly under pretense of the debate team's address. Beat: held breath — everything converges on one room, one moment, one choice.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Instead of celebrating, Orsen reads the erased names — Elias first — while Adaeze stands beside him holding the ledger, and Priya's exposé hits every phone in the gym. The board's silence breaks audibly. Beat: cathartic climax; truth spoken in the loudest room in the school.

chapters.title: Graduation, Unlocked
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue tone. Months later: the archive wing is rebuilt as a memorial, Elias's name restored to the honors wall, Adaeze consulted as historian. Orsen's relationship with his father is strained but honest, and his countdown calendar is blank — he stopped counting. Beat: quiet resolution; visibility chosen and kept.
